TEACHER EDUCATION PATHWAYS COURSE SYLLABUS
Education for personal renewal and social transformation.
A leading future-ready education university responsive to national and global development goals and directions
Philippine Normal University is committed to lead innovative, responsive and sustainable teacher education programs that set the standards of future-ready teachers and education leaders. As the National Center for Teacher Education, the Philippine Normal University commits to provide inclusive, innovative, impactful, and sustainable teacher education programs that produce future-ready teachers and education leaders imbued with the values of truth, excellence, and service. Furthermore, PNU shall ensure the continual improvement of its Quality Management System through compliance with International Quality Standards and statutory and regulatory requirements. PNU shall achieve these commitments through its core functions of instruction, research, extension, and production. Digitally Literate and Data-Driven Decision Maker Design Thinker and Innovator Discerning and Compassionate Person Dynamic Lifelong Learner and Leader Deeply Rooted Global Citizen The College of Teacher Development (CTD) is committed to champion quality teacher education in the country. It is dedicated to:
1. Provide future-ready teacher development through innovative, inclusive and quality-assured academic programs. 2. Lead in advancing teacher education research and translating scholarly work into relevant policies and practices that benefit education
and communities. 3. Establish CTD as leader in producing impactful educational resources, and programs. 4. Establish a robust international presence through strategic collaborations, advancing the College’s leadership in teacher education. 5. Maintain a pool of faculty experts who lead as influential public intellectuals in education and related disciplines. 6. Established well-defined systems-based solutions and sustainability practices to ensure efficiency and effectiveness of implementation
of CTD Programs and procedures.
1. Apply knowledge of educational philosophy and theories, current research in education, and professional ethics in teaching and learning practices critically.

Outcomes

2. Engage in reflective practice guided by the core values of effective teachers and continual professional learning, to promote positive societal transformation, and respond to the needs of an ever-changing world. TPROFED01
The Teaching Profession
None The course introduces the historical foundations, educational philosophies and the teachers’ professional ethics, rights, responsibilities, and core values that uphold the dignity of the teaching profession in the context of national and global teacher standards. In this course, pre-service teachers will be able to relate the historical development of education and the different Philosophies to the teaching-learning process in the present Philippine Educational System. In the end, the pre-service teachers are guided to build their own philosophy of education relevant to their professional role as teachers and reflective of their personal high regard for the teaching profession. They are expected to apply perceptive judgment, ethical and legal principles in analyzing cases related to the practice of the teaching profession and in making education-related decisions and principled action. Gender Inequality, Gender Literacy, Gender-fair Education

100%

PNU is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive academic environment for students from various backgrounds, including those with disabilities, exceptionalities, ethnic and linguistic differences, religious affiliations, gender identities, and other individual differences. The University ensures its commitment to equal access, participation, and engagement with educational opportunities that supports our academic culture and values as well as celebrate diversity and inclusivity.

If you have any physical or psychological/ mental health conditions or challenges which can affect your performance in class, you are encouraged to inform me. This is to ensure that we are creating and fostering a responsive classroom environment. You are also encouraged to avail of the services of the following offices regarding your challenge/ condition: - Student Affairs and Services Office: counselingservices@pnu.edu.ph - University Health Services Unit: uhsu@pnu.edu.ph - Gender, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusivity Office: gedio@pnu.edu.ph

he following course policies are to be presented and clarified to the class during the first session, if possible, of the school term:
1. Regular attendance and punctuality are to be strictly observed and monitored in all sessions. University policy on excessive absences (20%) is to be enforced unless these are valid and supported by appropriate documents. Coming to class after 15 minutes is considered late but not after 30 minutes. However, 2 consecutive tardiness would be equivalent to 1 absence. This would teach a valuable lesson on management of time, particularly punctuality, to prospective teachers and prevent distractions.
2. The nature of the course calls for active class participation from every student. Critical thinking is enhanced. This criterion is to be monitored and evaluated by the faculty with the aid of seat plan.
3. Examination will be announced. Failure to take it due to valid reason would be given a chance for make up. Otherwise, a failing grade would be given. The make-up should not extend beyond a week from the time student has reported back to the class unless there are special or unavoidable circumstances that would warrant an extension..
4. Paper presentation on assigned topics/problems should be accompanied by a handout on salient points and the use of audio-visual aids or technology. English is the medium of communication.
5. Deadline of submission of position paper is to be announced. No late submission is allowed to enable the faculty to submit final grade on time in conformity with the University policy.

6. Failure to comply with the course requirements would merit incomplete rating and this has to be completed within the next semester.
Students with Disability:
Students with disabilities who seek accommodations in a course must be registered with the OSASS and inform their instructors about their condition (visual acuity, functional vision, visual efficiency) at the beginning of the semester for accommodation services.
o Students with visual impairments (blindness and low vision) should first be oriented with the classroom environment, most especially with the gymnasium and laboratory equipment. They can also have their preferred seating.
o Tactile aids and manipulative materials (embossed relief maps and diagrams, three-dimensional (3D) models, tactile models) should be prepared for students with blindness. PowerPoint presentations, e-books and other materials preferably in Braille, must also be given to them ahead of time. Likewise, they should be allowed to use their assistive devices such as talking computers and calculators, iPad, audio recorders, smart phones, to serve as their notes in class discussions.
o For students with low vision, large-print books and handouts with large-print size scan be given to them ahead of time. o Teachers should talk in slow and clear manner, and most importantly should describe ALL discussions for students with visual
impairments. Instead of plainly writing on the board, the teacher should describe what is to be written or drawn on the board. This should also be done while presenting PowerPoint presentations, video clips, pictures and the like. o Extra time must be given to the students with disabilities as they travel from one class to the next. Sighted guides, preferably classmates, must be oriented and be allowed to help them in travelling. It is however recommended that students with disabilities become selfsufficient in travelling, most especially if they experienced a year of orientation and mobility in the university. o During examinations, teachers can prepare test papers in Braille for students with blindness. But if not possible, they can dictate the test items to the students or have one sighted guide to do the dictation while the teacher assists. For students with low vision, print materials could be prepared using large-print sizes (36-point type), in bold and black font, that are visible for them. o Teachers should model inclusive teaching among their students and therefore should NOT isolate any student, specifically those with disabilities from any class or school activity.
Proper accommodations must be prepared and consulted with experts in the discipline if needed. Wednesday, 8:00 – 10:00 AM Faculty Center Room 207
